sources.title: Evaluación de la vulnerabilidad ante el efecto del cambio climático: República Bolivariana de Venezuela
sources.organization: Ministry of Popular Power for Ecosocialism (MINEC), with FAO implementation support
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 assessment; projections for 2021–2040, 2041–2060 and 2061–2080, with 1970–2000 baseline.
sources.methodology: Sectoral projections use two GCMs and SSP2-4.5/SSP5-8.5.
sources.limitations: Full text read on user-uploaded Scribd mirror, not official host.

sources.title: Annual Report 2025: Chapter IV.B, Venezuela
sources.organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR), Organization of American States
sources.temporal_coverage: Annual human-rights monitoring for 2025; climate-event passages cover the first half of 2025.
sources.methodology: IACHR annual monitoring chapter synthesizes state statements, UN findings and cited reporting.
sources.limitations: Some environmental and event details are attributed to cited sources; this is not a climate-attribution study.

sources.title: Venezuela Situation Report No. 2 (Year-End), 31 December 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and UNICEF response from 1 January to 31 December 2024; issued 6 February 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF country situation report combines humanitarian monitoring and agency response data.
sources.limitations: Agency-reported reach and needs; not a population-wide impact evaluation or climate-attribution analysis.

sources.title: Venezuela Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1 (Mid-Year), 30 June 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and UNICEF response from 1 January to 30 June 2025; issued 1 August 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF country situation report combines humanitarian monitoring and agency response data.
sources.limitations: Agency-reported reach and needs; reported access constraints are contextual, not a causal evaluation.

claims.locator: Scribd-rendered report, printed pp.23–24, climate scenarios and projected precipitation section.
claims.paraphrase: Models project warming and generally declining, more seasonal rainfall, with regional increases in some months.
claims.limitations: Scenarios differ by model and region.

claims.locator: Scribd-rendered report, printed pp.26–27, agricultural vulnerability summary.
claims.paraphrase: High-vulnerability agricultural lands include Monagas, Miranda, Aragua, Carabobo, Cojedes, Portuguesa, Lara, Barinas, Táchira and Mérida.
claims.limitations: Risk classes are modelled, not observed losses.

claims.locator: Scribd-rendered report, printed p.44, Indigenous peoples sector, 2021–2040.
claims.paraphrase: Projected rainfall and heat anomalies affect Indigenous communities in Gran Sabana, Gran Guajira, Perijá, eastern Amazonas and Orinoco Delta.

claims.locator: Scribd-rendered report, printed p.25, projected climate impacts narrative.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment says floods may force displacement and climate impacts may weaken livelihoods, increasing poverty and urban inequality.
claims.scenario: General projected impacts; this passage does not assign an SSP.
claims.limitations: General conditional pathways, not quantified forecasts.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Floods may force displacement; climate impacts may weaken livelihoods and raise poverty/urban inequality, printed p.25.

claims.paraphrase: Tropical-wave rains affected Mérida, Táchira, Trujillo and Barinas; over 8,000 families were affected and rural isolation forced temporary internal relocation.
claims.limitations: IACHR reports hundreds, potentially thousands, temporarily relocated; exact count is unclear.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Rainfall and landslides isolated rural communities, forcing temporary internal relocation; ¶155.

claims.paraphrase: Warao communities feared Orinoco River rise could displace people; Amazonas authorities reported 200-plus families evacuated in July.
claims.limitations: The source does not establish that the evacuated families were Warao.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Warao expressed fear river rise would displace people; ¶156.

claims.paraphrase: IACHR, citing OHCHR, reports alleged illegal gold mining in Ye’kwana territories in Amazonas linked to violent clashes with mine-associated individuals.
claims.limitations: IACHR attributes the allegations to OHCHR; it does not connect mining violence to climate hazards.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Illegal mining in Ye’kwana territories allegedly led to violent clashes; ¶163, attributed to OHCHR.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.1, situation overview, paragraphs on 2024 tropical waves.
claims.paraphrase: Fifty-one tropical waves affected 47 municipalities in 17 states; over 75,200 people, including 28,400 children, were affected.
claims.limitations: National summary; municipality-level total is not disaggregated in this passage.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.1, situation overview, Sucre and Zulia flood details.
claims.paraphrase: Floods affected Montes, Valdez and Mejía in Sucre and Catatumbo, Colón and Rosario de Perijá in Zulia, including over 24,000 children.
claims.limitations: Reported affected-person counts; no household vulnerability breakdown.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.8–9, WASH response, climate and disaster-risk reduction, and local capacity sections.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF supported resilient water technologies and school disaster-risk learning; communities were trained to manage water systems, including in flood-affected Zulia and Sucre.
claims.limitations: Agency-reported delivery; the report does not evaluate long-term performance.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.1, situation overview, election-related unrest paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: Post-election civil unrest disrupted children’s access to essential services and increased protection risks; logistical and administrative barriers delayed lifesaving imports.
claims.limitations: The report does not state that unrest caused the flood impacts.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Post-election civil unrest disrupted services and increased child protection risks; report p.1.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.2, situation overview, early 2025 floods.
claims.paraphrase: Early rains affected 31 municipalities across ten states, damaging homes, schools, health facilities and services; over 37,000 people, including 13,600 children, were affected.
claims.limitations: These are agency-reported impacts through June 2025.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.4, health access and service constraints.
claims.paraphrase: Seasonal flooding combined with the electoral context to limit primary care access in border and hard-to-reach areas, disproportionately affecting women and children under five.
claims.limitations: UNICEF describes combined constraints; it does not isolate the flood’s effect.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Electoral context combined with seasonal flooding further limited primary-care access; report p.4.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.3, Indigenous health referrals and radio communication system.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF expanded radio referrals in three remote fluvial health facilities in Delta Amacuro for isolated Warao riverine communities.
claims.limitations: The report describes expansion, not measured outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.5, child protection and border displacement paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports ELN–Colombian army confrontations caused displacement and heightened child-protection risks in Táchira and Zulia border areas.
affected_groups: children and adolescents in border areas
claims.limitations: This FCV context is not linked by UNICEF to climate hazards.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Confrontations between ELN and Colombian army led to displacement and child-protection risks; report p.5.

search_audit.query: Venezuela climate vulnerability projections municipalities states indigenous communities drought flood official assessment
search_audit.outcome: Opened MINEC vulnerability assessment and IACHR monitoring; found modeled state/region exposures, Indigenous community projections and named flood-affected municipalities.

search_audit.query: Venezuela climate drought flood displacement livelihoods poverty services food insecurity official report
search_audit.outcome: MINEC describes conditional displacement and livelihood/poverty pathways; IACHR reports flood isolation and temporary relocation; UNICEF records flooding-related service constraints.

search_audit.query: Venezuela armed groups insecurity political violence barriers climate adaptation disaster response indigenous mining
search_audit.outcome: IACHR and UNICEF report mining-related violence and electoral/border constraints separately from climate hazards; no source reviewed states violence blocked climate adaptation specifically.

search_audit.query: Venezuela climate resilience adaptation early warning indigenous water systems capacity official report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF documents water-system training, resilient WASH technologies and Warao radio referrals; IACHR notes adaptation targets alongside a national adaptation-plan gap.

gaps: The reviewed evidence gives climate-linked displacement, service and livelihood pathways but no primary passage establishing climate hazards as a cause of armed conflict, mining violence or political unrest.
Searches found no source stating that insecurity specifically obstructed climate adaptation or early warning; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of no effect.
MINEC's full report text was accessible only through a user-uploaded Scribd mirror; official-host verification and reuse terms remain unresolved.
The 2025 IACHR climate chapter synthesizes attributed reporting rather than providing an independent climate-attribution analysis; UNICEF response figures are agency-reported.

Venezuela's 2024 climate transparency submission was not analyzed because the UNFCCC PDF exceeded the browser tool's accessible size; IOM and IFRC records tested were blocked or unsupported by the browser reader.
